issues.description: Method signature mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide: The problem statement (UML and textual description) and the template usage expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() that returns a String (e.g., Part 2: "The method messageOnRide() should return \"Riding on [Animal Type] [name]\""). The template Main.java calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and the implementing classes Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(String equipment). This parameter difference makes the API inconsistent across artifacts and will cause confusion or compilation errors when code (or tests) expects the no-arg version but finds a version requiring a String parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent with the problem statement and template by changing the method signature to a no-argument method: declare String messageOnRide() in Rideable and update Pig and Seal to implement public String messageOnRide() that returns the expected text (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle" or "Riding on Seal Clarabelle"). Alternatively, if the equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template code to document and call messageOnRide(String equipment) consistently; preferred fix is to align the solution to the original no-arg specification to match the UML and template usage.

issues.description: Concept: the animal 'ride' message method. Problem statement and template refer to a no-argument method named messageOnRide() that returns a String (the UML and Part 2 text and the template Main call use r.messageOnRide()). Solution repository defines a different API: interface Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implementations Pig.messageOnRide(String equipment) and Seal.messageOnRide(String equipment). This is an identifier / signature mismatch: the same conceptual operation is exposed under different method signatures across artifacts. A student following the problem description and template will expect and call messageOnRide() with no arguments, but the solution API requires a String parameter, causing confusion and compilation mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method signature for the ride message across all artifacts. Preferred fix (match problem & template): change the solution API to declare Rideable.messageOnRide() : String (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal to implement public String messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternative fix (if an equipment parameter is intended): update the problem statement text and UML to show messageOnRide(String equipment), update the example call in template Main to r.messageOnRide("<equipment>") and adapt the description to document the equipment parameter. Ensure all three places (problem_statement.md, template_repository Main, and solution_repository Rideable and implementations) use the same signature.
